title: Statement size measure
statement: For a natural number $F$, define the size of a statement recursively as follows. The skip statement has size $0$; an assignment has size the expression size plus $2$; a store has size the sum of its address and value expression sizes plus $1$; a sequence has size the sum of its parts; a conditional has size the condition size plus the two branch sizes plus $1$; a while loop has size the condition size plus the body size plus $1$; and a procedure call has size the sum of its argument expression sizes, plus $2F+7$. Here expression size is $2$ for a variable, the length measure of the binary digits for a constant (where the empty list has length measure $1$ and each digit contributes $1$ plus $1$ if it is nonzero), the sum of the two operand sizes plus $1$ for a binary operation, and the operand size plus $1$ for a load; condition size is the sum of its two expression sizes plus $3$ for a strict comparison and plus $4$ for equality.
